newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse seen rising, dealers worried.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse seen rising, dealers worried.

text.p: The blue-chip Bel-20 index rallied on Thursday to close more than one percent higher as investors continued to wallow in Belgian shares, with dealers seeing no near end to the bourse's bullish behaviour.
"The dollar has had a positive impact and there isn't anything moving in the wrong direction," said trader Patrick Millecam at brokerage Coluy & Co.
The Bel-20 closed up 1.34 percent at 2,075.06, having risen by over 200 points since the start of 1997.
But dealers expressed worries at the current bullish rises, fearing that when a drop hits the Bel-20 it will hit it hard.
"Everyone is feeling a bit uncomfortable that it (Bel-20) is rising so quickly," said one trader.
He added that nobody wanted to sell their shares even if they could take large profits.
"Whenever this sentiment turns down, there'll be many people at the selling side," he added.
Dealers believed the Bel-20 could reach 2,100 in coming weeks, but hoped this would be a signal to consolidate.
Kredietbank, the outstanding market performer of the day, jumped 6.14 percent to close at 12,100 francs after earlier setting a new high of 12,400 francs.
Dealers said the share which had lagged recent bourse rises was now catching up as investors shopped around for undervalued stocks.
"Everybody agrees that Kredietbank has lagged the rest of the banks in Belgium but I'm surprised by the sharp rise," said trader Patrick Millecam at brokerage Coluy & Co.
Generale Bank was another large gainer, rising 4.24 percent to 12,300 francs.
Cement maker CBR saw profit-taking after sharp climbs since November 1996. It closed down 4.41 percent to 3,250 francs.
